map.A percentages adventure in five chapters: A percentages story. Five parts. Six gates for you. Do the math to move the story.
map.Pattern distortion at the night market,: A pattern problem at the night market, crew. It smells like fake percents.
map.Previously: the crew won the Courier Cup: Before: the crew won the Courier Cup with ratio proof. Graphs don't lie. Then the autumn storm broke the old pier.
map.The storm cracked the pier in three plac: The storm cracked the pier in three places. Tonight's market has to pay for the repair. All of it.
map.So I built us a donation board. One hund: So I built us a donation board. One hundred bulbs. One for each block of the goal.
map.A hundred bulbs? That's literally a prog: A hundred bulbs? That's a progress bar. I respect it.
map.Warning: a stall by the gate is shouting: Look out: a stall by the gate shouts "50% OFF EVERYTHING". Its numbers feel… bent.
map.The market gate. A familiar smirk under: The market gate. A smirk we know. A very loud sign.
map.Half off, little library heroes. Fifty p: Half off, little heroes. Fifty percent! That's close to free.
map.\"Basically free\" from the guy who \"ba: "Close to free"? From the guy who "almost" won the Courier Cup? We'll check your tags, Bram.
map.Percent means \"per hundred.\" Your boar: Percent means "per hundred." Your board IS a hundred. 35 per 100 = 35%.
map.A percent is a ratio out of 100. On a 10: A percent is a ratio out of 100. On a 10×10 grid, each cell is 1%. So 35% is any 35 cells.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. L: Reader, you're our fifth crew member. Light the board to 35%!
map.The donation board has 100 bulbs — every: The donation board has 100 bulbs. Each bulb is 1% of the goal. Tonight the pier fund is at 35%. Tap bulbs to light exactly 35 (any 35 you like). Tap again to turn one off.
map.Conceptual: percent means PER HUNDRED —: Conceptual: percent means PER HUNDRED. The board is the hundred. 35% is just 35 bulbs out of 100. No more math needed.
map.Procedural: each full row is 10 bulbs =: Procedural: each full row is 10 bulbs = 10%. Light 3 full rows (30%). Then light 5 more bulbs to reach 35.
map.Three stalls, three weird tags. Which de: Three stalls, three odd tags. Which deal is biggest: 3/4, 0.75, or 75%?
map.Trick question. That's ONE number wearin: Trick question. That is ONE number in three disguises.
map.Unmask them: fraction → decimal, divide: Unmask them: fraction → decimal, divide top by bottom. Decimal → percent, multiply by 100. Slide the point two places right.
map.Fractions, decimals, and percents can na: Fractions, decimals, and percents can name the same value. Divide to get the decimal. Then × 100 to get the percent.
map.Reader — unmask every tag. Sort the disg: Reader, take off each tag's mask. Sort the tags into their families.
map.Six tag cards, three fraction families:: Six tag cards. Three fraction families: 3/4, 3/5, and 1/8. Tap a card to change its family (3/4 → 3/5 → 1/8 → unsorted). Put each card with the fraction of equal value.
map.Conceptual: a fraction, a decimal, and a: Conceptual: a fraction, a decimal, a percent: all can be the SAME value. They just wear new clothes. Divide top by bottom to see the decimal inside.
map.Procedural: 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75. Decimal → perc: Procedural: 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75. Decimal → percent: slide the point two places right. Test each card this way. Then sort it.
map.The crew's lantern stall. A line is form: The crew's lantern stall. A line is forming. No time for long division.
map.Boss request: 19% of our 52 boxed lanter: Boss request: 19% of our 52 boxed lanterns go to the gift bundles. Quick! About how many boxes?
map.Don't panic-divide. Use a benchmark: 10%: Don't panic-divide. Use a benchmark. 10% of anything is easy. Slide the decimal one place left.
map.19% is a breath away from 20% — and 20%: 19% is very close to 20%. And 20% is just two of those easy 10% chunks. Estimate. The line is long.
map.A benchmark is a friendly percent you ca: A benchmark is an easy percent. You can find it fast: 10%, 25%, 50%. Build hard percents from easy ones.
map.Speed round, reader — about how many lan: Quick round, reader. About how many lantern boxes?
map.Gift bundles get 19% of the 52 boxed lan: Gift bundles get 19% of the 52 boxed lanterns. The line is long. Don't find it exactly. Use the 10% benchmark and pick the best estimate.
map.Conceptual: 19% is almost 20%, and 20% i: Conceptual: 19% is almost 20%, and 20% is just TWO easy 10% chunks. Estimate with easy numbers.
map.Procedural: 10% of 52 — slide the decima: Procedural: 10% of 52. Slide the decimal one place left: 5.2. Now double that for about 20%.
map.Our sale is REAL. Thirty percent off the: Our sale is REAL. Thirty percent off the storm lantern. The tag shows the work.
map.30% means 30 per 100 — so the discount i: 30% means 30 per 100. So the discount is 0.30 of the price. Multiply, then subtract.
map.Honest tags list both numbers: the disco: Honest tags show both numbers. The discount is what you don't pay. The sale price is what you do pay. Bram's tags show… vibes.
map.A discount is the part you don't pay: di: A discount is the part you don't pay: discount = percent × full price. Sale price = full price − discount.
map.Fill in the honest tag, reader — custome: Fill in the honest tag, reader. People squint at it.
map.The storm lantern costs $45 and is 30% o: The storm lantern costs $45 and is 30% off. Finish the honest tag: the discount in dollars, and the sale price.
map.Conceptual: 30% means 30 per 100 — as a: Conceptual: 30% means 30 per 100. As a decimal, 0.30. The discount is that decimal TIMES the whole price.
map.Procedural: discount = 45 × 0.3 (watch t: Procedural: discount = 45 × 0.3. Watch the decimal point. Sale price = 45 minus the discount.
map.Twenty-five beats twenty, math kid. Mine: Twenty-five beats twenty, math kid. Mine's the better deal. Count on it.
Percents don't shop, Bram. Dollars shop. Take a big percent off a big price. It can still cost more.
map.Strategy: 25% off means you pay 75%. 20%: Plan: 25% off means you pay 75%. 20% off means you pay 80%. Find what leaves your pocket. Then compare.
map.To compare deals, find each final price:: To compare deals, find each final price: pay (100% − discount%) of the full price. Then pick the smaller number.
map.Run both tags, reader. Which stall actua: Do both tags, reader. Which stall really saves us money?
map.Same tea set, two stalls. Bram: 25% off: Same tea set, two stalls. Bram: 25% off $32. Harbor stall: 20% off $29. Find BOTH final prices. Then pick the better deal.
map.Conceptual: a bigger percent off a bigge: Conceptual: take a big percent off a big price. It can still cost more. The winner is the smaller FINAL price. That is the dollars you pay.
map.Procedural: 25% off means you pay 75%: 3: Procedural: 25% off means you pay 75%: 32 × 0.75. 20% off means you pay 80%: 29 × 0.80. Then compare.
map.Closing hour. The pier fund thermometer: Closing time. The pier fund chart reads $720. Bram's sign glows like a dare.
map.$18 off a $60 tag is NOT half. Work back: $18 off a $60 tag is NOT half. Work backwards: the whole = part ÷ percent.
map.And our $720? That's 90% of the goal. Sa: And our $720? That is 90% of the goal. The same backwards move finds the finish line.
map.The whole is the original 100%. Know a p: The whole is the first 100%. Know a part and its percent? Divide: whole = part ÷ (percent as a decimal).
map.BOSS GATE. Four locks. Percents only tel: BOSS GATE. Four locks. Percents are true only if the whole is honest.
map.Bram's sign: \"You save $18 — that's 50%: Bram's sign: "You save $18 — that's 50% OFF!" But the price tag reads $60. Meanwhile the pier fund holds $720 — exactly 90% of the goal. Four locks:
map.IF $18 really were 50%, the original pri: IF $18 were 50%, the full price would be: 18 ÷ 0.5 = $
map.What percent of the $60 tag is the $18 d: What percent of the $60 tag is the $18 discount?
map.The crew's verdict for the market counci: What the crew tells the market council:
map.$720 is 90% of the pier goal. Goal = 720: $720 is 90% of the pier goal. Goal = 720 ÷ 0.9 = $
map.Conceptual: every lock is the same move: Conceptual: every lock is the same move. A percent ties a PART to its WHOLE. Know any two, and division finds the third.
map.Procedural: whole = part ÷ (percent as a: Procedural: whole = part ÷ (percent as a decimal). Real percent = part ÷ whole, then × 100. Locks 1 and 4 divide by the percent. Lock 2 divides part by whole.
map.Every bulb lit. One hundred out of one h: Every bulb lit. One hundred out of one hundred. The pier gets fixed!
map.Market council made Bram repaint his sig: The market council made Bram repaint his sign: "30% off." The truth at last, in percent form.
New problem. It looks like… plans. To be continued…
map.Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks t: Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks the next question. This volume: worked backwards from a part to find the whole.
map.Evidence officer. Allergic to \"basicall: Proof keeper. Hates "close to free." This volume: showed a big percent can be a worse deal.
map.Builder and maker. This volume: built th: Builder and maker. This volume: built the hundred-bulb gift board. Priced the stall fairly.
map.Pattern hunter. This volume: estimated w: Pattern hunter. This volume: did fast guesses with 10% benchmarks. Faster than the line could grumble.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A part of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Senses problems. Cannot do math. That's your job.
map.Percent.A ratio out of 100. On a hundred: Percent.A ratio out of 100. On a hundred grid, 35 cells lit = 35%.
map.Benchmarks.10% of a number: slide the de: Benchmarks.10% of a number: slide the decimal one place left. Stack benchmarks to estimate: 19% ≈ two 10% chunks.
map.Percent of a number.30% of $45 = 0.30 ×: Percent of a number.30% of $45 = 0.30 × 45 = $13.50 off. Then: sale price = whole − discount.
map.Find the whole.Whole = part ÷ percent. $: Find the whole.Whole = part ÷ percent. $720 is 90% of the goal → 720 ÷ 0.9 = $800.
"A percent is a promise about a whole. Always ask: a hundred of WHAT?" — A.V.
map.completed Volume 4: The Hundred Market a: finished Volume 4: The Hundred Market. Can do percents as per-100. Can match fraction, decimal, and percent. Can use benchmarks. Can find percent of a number. Can find the whole.
Thank you for keeping the market honest. Volume 5 waits at the Brightside lot.
map.A different board shows 60% on its hundr: A different board shows 60% on its hundred grid.
map.60% means 60 per 100 — so exactly 60 of: 60% means 60 per 100. So exactly 60 of the 100 cells get shaded.
map.Fast way: 6 full rows of 10. Check: 60/1: Fast way: 6 full rows of 10. Check: 60/100 = 60%.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.On a 100-square grid, how many squares s: On a 100-square grid, how many squares show 80%?
map.10% of 38 = 3.8 (slide the decimal one p: 10% of 38 = 3.8 (slide the decimal one place left).
map.Sale price = 20 − 8 = $12. The tag shows: Sale price = 20 − 8 = $12. The tag shows both numbers.
map.Stall A: 50% off an $18 mug → pay 18 × 0: Stall A: 50% off an $18 mug → pay 18 × 0.5 = $9.
Stall B: 30% off a $12 mug → pay 12 × 0.7 = $8.40.
map.$8.40 < $9 — the SMALLER percent wins be: $8.40 < $9. The SMALLER percent wins. Why? The whole was smaller.
map.You buy a $40 item at 10% off. What do y: You buy a $40 item at 10% off. What do you pay? (number only)
map.Another sign brags: 'save $9 — that's 50: Another sign brags: 'save $9 — that's 50% off!' on a $45 tag.
map.If $9 were really 50%, the whole would b: If $9 were really 50%, the whole would be 9 ÷ 0.5 = $18. The tag says $45. That does not fit.
map.Real percent: 9 ÷ 45 = 0.2 → 20%. The si: Real percent: 9 ÷ 45 = 0.2 → 20%. The sign said 50. Busted.
map.35 of 100 bulbs — exactly 35%. The board: 35 of 100 bulbs: exactly 35%. The board glows and the crowd cheers!
map.At least one card is in the wrong family: At least one card is in the wrong family. Divide top by bottom. Check the value, not the look.
map.Pick an estimate first — the line is gro: Pick an estimate first. The line is growing.
map.10% of 52 ≈ 5.2, doubled ≈ 10.4 — about: 10% of 52 ≈ 5.2, doubled ≈ 10.4. About 10 boxes. Bundles packed before the line blinked.
map.That's only ONE 10% chunk. 19% is nearly: That is only ONE 10% chunk. 19% is nearly TWO of them.
map.26 is half of 52 — that's the 50% benchm: 26 is half of 52. That is the 50% benchmark. Is 19% anywhere near half?
map.20 boxes would be almost 40% of 52. How: 20 boxes would be almost 40% of 52. How big is one 10% chunk of 52?
map.$13.50 off, $31.50 to pay — an honest ta: $13.50 off, $31.50 to pay. An honest tag. Three lanterns sell in a minute.
map.The discount lock holds. Multiply 45 by: The discount lock holds. Multiply 45 by 0.3. Mind where the decimal lands.
map.Discount's right! Sale price = original: Discount's right! Sale price = full price minus discount. Take it from $45.
map.$23.20 beats $24. The smaller percent wo: $23.20 beats $24. The smaller percent won. Bram's jaw drops 100%.
map.Check the final prices: pay (100% − disc: Check the final prices: pay (100% − discount%) of each full price. Try 0.75 × 32 and 0.80 × 29.
map.Your prices are right… now which FINAL p: Your prices are right. Now which FINAL price is less? That is where the money goes.
map.Lock 1 holds. Whole = part ÷ percent. Di: Lock 1 holds. Whole = part ÷ percent. Dividing by 0.5 (a half) makes the number DOUBLE.
map.Lock 2 holds. 18 ÷ 60 gives a decimal —: Lock 2 holds. 18 ÷ 60 gives a decimal. Then slide it two places right. Now it is a percent.
map.Lock 3 holds. Compare your Lock 2 percen: Lock 3 holds. Compare your Lock 2 percent to the sign's 50%. Do they match?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. $18 of $60 is 30%, not 5: ALL LOCKS OPEN. $18 of $60 is 30%, not 50. Sign repainted! And 720 ÷ 0.9 = the $800 goal… MET. THE PIER IS SAVED!
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
